title: Design Choices
text: vignette outlines key design decisions behind UNO game simulation package. explains choices function names, argument structures, user workflow, internal helper functions, use custom vector classes (vctrs). also highlight limitations, alternative designs considered, generative AI (ChatGPT) supported development. special note end addresses avoid known C++ issues development.

title: Design Choices
text: selected clear self-explanatory function names reflect function’s purpose — especially important beginners exploring game simulation R. create_uno_deck(): Builds full UNO deck number, action, wild cards. deal_hands(): Shuffles deck deals 7 cards player, returning initial hands, draw pile, first discard card. play_turns_loop(): Handles core logic turn--turn gameplay using dealt hands draw/discard piles. play_game(): wrapper function sets runs full game end--end. summarise_hand(): helper count many cards suit (color) player . card_suit(): Extracts color/suit card_vctr object. new_card_vctr(): Constructor custom card_vctr class. function one thing clearly named match human describe task casual conversation — deal cards, play turns, summarize hands, etc.

title: Design Choices
text: Arguments across package simple consistent, prioritizing ease use: functions require intuitive inputs like deck, n_players, hands. provide default values practical, e.g., n_players = 4 deal_hands() play_game(), make running sample game easy without custom setup. Validation enforced within functions ensure arguments right type (e.g., deck must tibble/data.frame, n_players must numeric ≥ 2). choices make package beginner-friendly robust user error.

title: Design Choices
text: ’s typical user interact UNO package, step step: Create UNO deck: Use create_uno_deck() generate complete, shuffled UNO deck standard number, action, wild cards. Deal cards players: Call deal_hands(deck, n_players = 4) distribute 7 cards player, start discard pile, return draw pile. typically first step game. Play game: Use play_game(n_players = 4) simulate complete UNO game, including card dealing, turn--turn play, automatic handling draw/discard piles. Run gameplay manually (advanced users): control, advanced users can use deal_hands() pass result play_turns_loop() manual gameplay simulation. Analyze hands (optional): Use summarise_hand(hands, player) count many cards suit (color) specific player — useful custom rules strategy analysis. Explore card structure: Use helper functions like card_suit() work card_vctr class directly inspect manipulate card content programmatically. design makes UNO package flexible casual users — can simulate game one line — advanced users, can build gameplay logic extensions.
